Nothing here changes the frozen metrics.

order: official policy or regulation (Faculty Handbook, University by-laws)
official system manual of the issuing unit (ITC or HR guides)
source_precedence_proposal.rule: policy facts (entitlements, limits, approvals, obligations) come from the policy source; interface steps, menu paths, URLs and system contacts come from the newest official system manual; a third-party document is never a source for a UOS policy or a UOS procedure; a conflict between two official sources is reported, never averaged
source_precedence_proposal.implementation_note: no precedence rule is implemented in PF-1; the registry's authority field already exists and can carry an authority_level in PF-2

additions_for_multi_document: printed_page (when the printed number differs from the PDF page)
subsection (when a guide has its own section map)
document_type (policy, system_manual, procedure, training, faq, vendor)
language (en, ar, en+ar) and page_language for bilingual pages
domain hint (primary specialist) as a routing aid, not a routing decision
procedure_step index and parent_section for step chunks
source_hash (SHA-256 of the file) for content identity
metadata_requirements.backward_compatibility: every existing key keeps its name and meaning; the handbook's records are unchanged; new keys default to null for the handbook so the frozen specialists and the I-7 interface read the same values as today

supports_today.procedures: as paragraph windows and rows, no step chunk
supports_today.source-specific citations: source_title per chunk; the interface shows one document chip

reasons: pdf_loader.find_pdf_file loads the first PDF in data/ and KnowledgeBase holds one pdf_file: a second document is never loaded
retrieval._cache_paths keys the embedding cache by that one file name; a corpus of several documents needs a corpus-level cache key
the section map applies to one source (page_count check); other documents get chapter and section nulls unless each gets its own map
DOCX is not readable by the loader (4 of 25 candidates); conversion to PDF or a DOCX reader is needed
no page-language detection: bilingual guides would index garbled Arabic pages next to the English ones

the four frozen specialists compile their retrieval scope with the handbook's source id and page ranges (compile_scope in each specialist), so chunks of any other source never reach a specialist; RetrievalScope combines its constraints with AND, so a handbook-pages OR new-source scope is not expressible; serving new documents through Plan F needs either a scope-extension seam in non-frozen code (retrieval.py and plan_f_runtime.py) or a decision record reopening the specialists
ui/presentation.source_chips shows one document chip (the first item's title); several sources need one chip per source

the legacy path (orchestrator, retrieval without scope) would search every indexed chunk, so new documents reach the legacy answer immediately after ingestion; this is where the first PF-2 measurement can be made

chunking_readiness.current: paragraph windows over sentence splits (PARA_CHUNK_SIZE_WORDS with overlap), one row per visual line, row windows over consecutive rows, OCR chunks when enabled
fits: table rows (appraisal tables, grade-transfer steps as rows)
contact lines (rows with phones or e-mails)
weak: numbered procedures: the sentence splitter breaks '1. Log in to Blackboard' at the step number, and a step with sub-bullets spreads over several rows
FAQ or message/meaning/action tables: rows lose the header pairing
bilingual pages: English and Arabic rows interleave
smallest_safe_extension: procedure_step chunks: a numbered or lettered step with its continuation lines as one chunk, with step index and the heading above it as parent_section
procedure_window chunks: three consecutive steps as one chunk, like row_window
page_language filter before chunking: skip pages whose Arabic share exceeds a threshold, or mark them language=ar
no FAQ-pair or navigation-path chunk type is needed for the approved set (no FAQ document; menu paths sit inside steps)
